incident: NetWalker ransomware in 1 hour (RDP admin login to domain-wide NetWalker)

sources.title: NetWalker Ransomware in 1 Hour - The DFIR Report (2020-08-31)
sources.what_it_gave: entry (RDP with valid DomainName\Administrator), hop (RDP from first host to a DC after cred dump, then PsExec DC->all domain-joined), cred access (procdump lsass + Mimikatz), impact (NetWalker via PsExec+PowerShell to all online hosts), 1h

narrative_before: In this 2020 honeypot-environment intrusion the DFIR Report observed a threat actor log in over RDP with a valid 'DomainName\Administrator' account (source assessed as 198.181.163[.]103). About 16 minutes after login the actor dropped and ran c37.ps1 (assessed Cobalt Strike), then used procdump64.exe on lsass followed by Mimikatz to dump credentials. The actor RDPed into a domain controller, dropped ip.list.txt, P100119.ps1 and PsExec, and used PsExec as the Domain Administrator to deploy NetWalker (P100119.ps1 via PowerShell) to all online domain-joined systems. The entire intrusion took about one hour; the operators demanded $50k rising to $100k.

detection_moments.description: RDP login with valid Administrator account; ~16 min later c37.ps1 (Cobalt Strike) executed on the beachhead.
detection_moments.evidence: 'the threat actor logged in using the DomainName\Administrator account ... About 16 minutes after this login, c37.ps1 was dropped and run' - NetWalker in 1 Hour, The DFIR Report

detection_moments.description: LSASS dumped with procdump + Mimikatz on the beachhead; actor RDPs into a domain controller and stages PsExec + P100119.ps1.
detection_moments.evidence: 'procdump64.exe -ma lsass.exe lsass.dmp, followed by Mimikatz ... RDPed into a Domain Controller after dumping credentials' - NetWalker in 1 Hour

attack_path: RDP login with valid DomainName\Administrator account (T1078/T1021.001)
RDP from beachhead to a domain controller after LSASS credential dump (T1021.001/T1003.001)
PsExec from the DC mounting shares as Domain Administrator, running P100119.ps1/NetWalker on all online domain-joined systems (T1021.002/T1486)
ambiguities: Honeypot environment; hosts named by role only, no sector.
Encryption order across hosts not stated; generic domain-joined systems modelled as srv_1/pc_2/pc_3.
How domain-admin access was obtained beyond the dumped credentials is not described.
No defender detection timeline; moments are the report's activity markers.
